claims.text: For the meaning of his name refer to Húrin of Emyn Arnen - Etymology. Húrin II was probably named after the hero of the First Age Húrin Thalion, the Lord of Dor-lómin.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part Two. Body, Mind and Spirit: V. Beards", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021, footnote 3, p. 189; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "VII. The Heirs of Elendil", p. 203

claims.text: Húrin ruled Gondor as its Steward for twenty-three years, and was succeeded by his son, Belecthor I.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Southern Line: Heirs of Anarion"
